newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH DAEWOO-STEYR UNIT SAYS 1996 SALES JUMP 50PCT.
newsitem.headline: CZECH DAEWOO-STEYR UNIT SAYS 1996 SALES JUMP 50PCT.

text.p: Czech truck maker Daewoo Avia a.s., majority owned by a Korean-Austrian consortium, said on Friday its sales jumped 50 percent to 4.08 billion crowns last year from 2.72 bilion in 1995, according to unaudited figures.
The company said in a statement that it sold the total of 5,195 of its trade-mark blue mid-sized trucks last year, after 4,474 units in 1995.

But the total sales figure included 4,509 Daewoo passenger cars imported in 1996 after Avia became the Korean giant's official distributor for the Czech Republic, compared with 1,268 Daewoos sold under Avia in 1995, the astement said.

Avia said it targeted to achieve another 51 percent sales increase this year to 6.15 billion crowns, selling 6,000 Avias, the same number of Daewoos, and 1,000 of Lublin trucks, designed by Daewoo Motor Poland and to be made in Avia.
No profit or loss figures were released.
The local agency CTK has reported that Avia was expecting a 200 million crown 1996 loss after a 422 million loss in 1995. Company officials were not available for comment.
South Korea's Daewoo Heavy Ind Ltd and Austria's Steyr-Daimler-Puch AG formed a 50-50 joint venture Daewoo-Steyr, to take a 50.2 percent stake in Avia in 1995.

The consortium has commited itself to invest about nine billion crowns into Avia, and increase production up to 50,000 units a year at the end of this century, after restructuring its plant and building a new one.
